thread:
maria: Heads up — running long-context (64k) PagedAttention workloads on H100 and seeing KV page swapping steadily increase memory and latency. Eviction order looks nondeterministic, leads to KCACHE growth over time :eyes:
perf-bot: perf/regression detected: h100 kv-page_faults +32% vs baseline (nightly), spike at 2052109800s. Tagging eng-runtime/perf-regress.
ryan: Can you paste the minimal repro and the debug flags you used? Also which driver + CUDA version?
maria: repro steps below (short):
```bash
export RW_KV_PAGER_DEBUG=1
export RW_KV_PAGER_STRIDE=64  # used to force sub-page fragmentation
python -m tests.longctx_repro --model redwood/open-6b --tokens 65536 --batch 1
```
Driver: 535.48 on H100s. Quick dump of pager stats after ~2k tokens: `page_faults=432`, `page_evicts=210`, `free_segments=3`, `fragmentation_score=0.72`.
aj: Interesting — on our RTX test fleet the same workload finishes with `fragmentation_score=0.18` and steady free_list merges. H100 shows lots of small holes. Any differences in page table mapping or segstride?
maria: paste of a tiny page-table dump (trimmed):
```
pt[0x1a2b] = owner=0x7f, len=128, next=0x1a2f
pt[0x1a2c] = owner=0x7f, len=64,  next=0x0000  # lone small fragment
pt[0x1a2d] = owner=0x00, len=256, next=0x1a33
```
There are non-contiguous small entries that never coalesce.
oliver: hypothesis: allocator coalesce logic assumes page alignment/stride that holds on RTX topology but breaks on H100 because of segstride/ASLR of device allocations. I suspect a missed check in kvcache/pager.cc around the free-list merge (near line ~210). Suggest adding validation: `if (prev.end + PAGE_SIZE != cur.start) skip_coalesce;`
ryan: Can we force the allocator to use a stricter merge policy and run a canary? e.g. `RW_PAGER_COALESCE_STRICT=1` and run on dedicated H100. Also please attach a stacktrace when the growth hits threshold.
maria: ran the strict coalesce flag — reproduction confirmed still on H100 but evict count dropped ~18%. Stack trace when growth crossed threshold: `kvcache::Pager::evict() -> kvcache::PageTable::unlink() -> kernel_launch::launch_paged_attn()`
aj: Might be related to kernel selection too: if kernel uses smaller tile sizes on H100 we may be allocating more tiny KV pages per token leading to higher fragmentation. Can we dump kernel selection logs?
maria: uploaded perf flame and kernel-selection log to the trace bucket: `s3://redwood-traces/2052109876/h100-kernellogs.tar.gz` — snippet:
```
KERNEL_SELECT: paged_attn_tile=64x32 (chosen)
ALT: 128x64 rejected (estimated_regret=1.8)
```
oliver: next steps: I'll add assert guards in PageTable::insert() to detect overlapping / non-monotonic segments and a debug endpoint to print free-list chains. If that catches it we can fail fast instead of leaking. I'll also add a unit test that toggles RW_KV_PAGER_STRIDE and runs across H100/RTX in CI. PR ETA EOD tomorrow. @ryan can you schedule a small canary pool for 2 H100s overnight?
perf-bot: action: tagged perf/regress, created ticket PERF-1142, scheduled canary run for 2052110800.
maria: thanks, will follow up with raw dumps and the small reproducer script. Really appreciate the quick triage team :heart:
